source: Marathon Excellence 18-week web PDF (marathonexcellence.com, imperial), cross-checked against Kindle screenshots; PDF wins on conflicts
recommended_for: Running a PR; marathoners with two or more years of experience; post-collegiate middle-distance runners; runners aiming for time qualifiers at major-city marathons (e.g. Boston, London).
experience: Two or more years of marathon training experience.
structural_features: Occasional second midweek quality session (primary Tuesday workout + secondary Thursday workout in weeks 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10).
Kenyan-style progression run as a recurring staple session (weeks 1, 2, 6, 8, 10, 17).

Pace basis is % of 5k pace through the general phase; fitness estimate converts to % of marathon pace at the end of week 8, and the supportive phase paces off an initial MP estimate from week 9 onward.
Float-recovery cruise intervals (repeats with 400m float at 80% 5k instead of jogs) in weeks 7 and 9.
Alternating-kilometer sessions (fast km / float km) in weeks 11, 13, 14, 16, 17.
Stepwise long fast runs (progressing pace stage by stage) in weeks 11 and 15.
Down weeks at weeks 4, 8, and 12 with reduced mileage and fewer workouts.
Fitness-estimate revision markers at the end of weeks 2, 4, 8, 11, 13, and 16.
Peak mileage (55 / 65 mi) held across weeks 9-11 and week 13.
Race-day options: longer races (8k to half marathon) may replace weekend long runs on select weeks; race-week and pre-race Sunday workouts adapt to Saturday vs Sunday marathon dates.

weeks.notes: Marathon-specific phase begins. Wednesday is a front-loaded cut-down interval session (3 km / 2 km / 2 km / 1 km, descending pace); precise pacing matters less than bringing the effort down across the workout. Saturday is 6 x (3 km at 100% MP, 1 km at 85% MP), a long look at what marathon pace feels like for extended blocks, on race-specific terrain with race-day fueling. Mileage now matters less than recovering well between workouts.

weeks.notes: Recovery is the priority after last weekend's big session; keep early-week runs on the short end of the range if you're still fatigued. Wednesday's fast continuous run is regenerative: adjust the distance, not the pace, to keep it at 7/10. Saturday's stepwise long fast run is the toughest workout of the plan; fuel and dress exactly as on race day and focus on the structure of the stages rather than percentage-perfect pacing.

weeks.notes: Early-week easy-to-moderate days set up Thursday's final full workout: alternating kilometers with a faster 90% MP float. Since fitness is so specialized now, 103% MP may be all you can manage for the fast segments as long as the floats feel like true recovery; take gels mid-workout. Keep the taper at the upper end of the mileage range unless you know from experience that a bigger drop works better for you.

weeks.notes: Race week. Wednesday's session stays controlled like the general-phase cruise intervals: start at 104% MP and only work down to 107% if it still feels easy. Adjust the length of your runs in the final three days based on feel. The marathon itself won't ask anything you haven't practiced; follow the same rhythms and routines from training and you'll be on your way to a great race.
